name: Ambient 3D world loop
description: A fixed full-viewport WebGL scene idles on a clock with no input: a room, a slope of terrain, a water plane or a table of props, drawn in flat palette colours (ground tone, one mid tone, one accent). Slow things move: 80-300 dust motes drifting at 2-6px per second, a few flat translucent light planes sweeping over 20-40s, ripples, or a camera drift of 1-2% amplitude on a 12-20s sine. The page text scrolls over it in plain sections, and long copy sits on filled cards so legibility never depends on the scene; hero text at 72-120px, centred or bottom-left. The loop pauses when the tab is hidden or the canvas is off screen. Colour roles: ground = the scene's dominant tone, ink contrasting, accent = one lit object or the button.
phone: Particle count cut by 60%, pixel ratio 1.5, camera drift off; with reduced motion render one still frame.
houseRuleCheck: Light shafts and fog stay flat translucent planes, no gradient fill, no glow; text never sits in an outlined box over the scene, only on filled cards.

name: Bent planes on a ring
description: Seven to twelve portrait picture cards (3:4, about 320x430 on screen) are mapped onto planes bent around a ring, arc or spiral in WebGL (radius 1200-1800px, cards facing outward). The centred card is full size and its neighbours recede with depth, darker, at 0.55 opacity and up to 3px of depth blur. Input: the section is a held stage of about half a screen of scroll per card; each time the scroll crosses the next step the ring turns one card over 900ms (ease-out-expo), and two filled 56px circle buttons (ink fill) and the arrow keys do the same. The wheel is never captured, and the ring rests still between steps. The centred card's 40px title and 17px line sit beneath in DOM text on the ground, and a click opens it. Colour roles: flat ground, ink, accent on the arrows.
phone: Native scroll steps it, radius 900px, five cards visible; with reduced motion a flat native snap row of the same cards.
houseRuleCheck: No counter or index between cards and no drag cue; pictures must not be documentary photographs; no text boxes on the cards.

name: Scroll camera flight
description: One fixed full-viewport WebGL canvas sits behind the page and holds a continuous world (terrain, a corridor of columns, a field of objects, a city of blocks built from plain geometry or a few loaded models). A camera flies through it on a baked spline: page progress 0-1 over 6-8 screens of scroll maps to the spline position through a 0.06-0.1 lerp so it glides. The world is lit flat: ground, fog and sky are palette tones, with fog covering 30-80% of the camera range for depth. Text beats of 3-8 words at 56-96px sit over the canvas at one stop per screen, so no held screen is empty, each fading in over 0.6 of a screen and out over 0.4; the last stop carries one filled button. Budget under 150k triangles and compressed textures. Colour roles: ground = the fog tone, ink contrasting, accent = one lit object plus the button.
phone: Pixel ratio capped at 1.5, fewer objects, scroll length cut to about 60%; beats 36-48px; with reduced motion show a still frame and the beats as ordinary sections.
houseRuleCheck: Keep fog and sky flat tones, no gradient sky, glow or glass; text beats sit straight on the canvas with no box and over a calm part of the frame so they stay readable.

name: Chapter scene backdrop
description: A fixed WebGL layer sits behind all sections. Four to six chapters, each 100-150vh tall, own one scene built from instanced image planes, cut-outs or type glyphs: a drifting field of tiles, a low landscape of cut-outs, a swarm of words. Scenes regroup rather than cut: the instances tween for 1.2-1.6s (ease-in-out) into the next layout when the next chapter crosses the middle of the screen, while the ground tone cross-fades to the chapter's tone. DOM text scrolls over it: chapter statements at 56-96px, 20px body at max 44 characters per line, 160px of space between chapters. Colour roles: ground changes per chapter within a three-tone palette, ink flips light or dark with it (contrast 7:1 or better), accent = one instanced colour.
phone: Instance count x0.4, pixel ratio 1.5, same chapters with statements at 36-44px; with reduced motion swap scenes by a 200ms fade.
houseRuleCheck: Instances are image planes, cut-outs or glyphs; loose decorative discs, blobs and drawn shapes are dropped; tones change flat, never as a gradient.

name: Click camera dive
description: A 3D scene (a gallery of frames, a row of doors, a shelf of objects, a miniature town) rests in a slow idle drift. Clicking an object tweens the camera along a baked path into it over 1.2-3s (ease-in-out, up to 8s for a dramatic entry) while the others fade to the ground tone, and it ends on a flat detail scene holding a 56-80px headline, a 19px line and one filled button. A text Back link returns by the reverse path in 1.2s. Hovered objects lift 4% with the cursor. Colour roles: ground = the scene's flat tone, objects supply the colour, ink contrasting, accent on the button only.
phone: Tap to dive over 1.2s, pixel ratio 1.5; with reduced motion cut instead of travelling.
houseRuleCheck: Flat ground and fog, no glow and no gradient sky; the overlay text sits directly on the flat detail scene with no box on a photograph.

name: Click weather switch
description: A 100vh section with a live 3D world and a choice of three states. Scene: a flat-shaded low-poly terrain with one landmark object centred, one flat sky colour and linear fog toward that colour, camera fixed at a 12-degree look-down. Controls: three filled pills (56px high, 24px side padding, 12px apart) bottom centre, each naming a state (for example clear, mist, snow); the active pill is ink-filled, the others tinted. On click, over 1.6s: sky and fog colour lerp to the new state's colours, fog density lerps (0.012 to 0.04), the world rotates 25 degrees about the vertical axis, a particle layer fades in (snow flakes or rain streaks, 800 instanced points); there is no lightning flash. Colour roles: each state is one sky colour plus one fog colour; the page ground stays the section's own.
phone: Pills in equal thirds across the bottom, 52px high, 32px above the safe area; 250 particles; pixel ratio capped at 1.5.
houseRuleCheck: Sky is one flat colour per state (no gradient skybox) and fog is only a depth cue; no glass, no text boxes over the scene.

name: Clock day-night cycle
description: A modelled 3D diorama (one cluster of objects on a base, 100svh stage) is lit by four presets keyed to the visitor's local clock: day (6-17h), dusk (17-20h), night (20-5h), dawn (5-6h), with light colour, fog colour and rim colour cross-fading over 20-40s at the boundaries (a four-minute accelerated loop when demonstrating). The page follows: day is a light ground with dark ink, night a dark ground with light ink, dusk and dawn use the accent as the ground. Every colour is flat per preset; the fog is a flat colour equal to the ground and there is no gradient sky. At night stars appear as 1-2px points and lamps light up; small objects (birds, boats, steam) loop. The camera holds with a +-2 degree idle drift. A single headline of 2-5 words at the h1 step sits at the left. Phone: 0.75 pixel ratio, static camera.
phone: 0.75 pixel ratio, static camera.
houseRuleCheck: Clean with discipline: no gradient sky or fog, lighting only; the four presets stay in one palette family (ground, ink, accent) so there is no colour sprawl. Needs a modelled asset, not a drawn illustration.

name: Disc mask world reveal
description: A 3D world (a floor and 6-12 objects) is visible only inside a circular mask at the canvas centre; outside it the canvas is the flat ground. On load the mask radius grows from 0 to about 60 percent of the viewport height (diameter) in 1.2s on ease-out-expo, with no overshoot, and then rests. On click or press it widens again to cover the full screen over 1.6s while the camera pulls back by 20 percent, revealing the whole world; a second click closes it. The mask edge is a crisp cut with no glow and no outline. A solid pill below the disc says what to do in sentence case (Press to open, 16px). The cursor shows a press state while waiting. Phone: disc diameter 80 percent of the width, tap to widen.
phone: Disc 80 percent of the width, tap to widen.
houseRuleCheck: Clean with a crisp edge: a glowing rim would be a glow and an outline, so the edge is a plain mask cut, and the disc neither overshoots nor breathes. The world is modelled 3D, not a drawn illustration.

name: Hotspot model explorer
description: A pinned stage of about 300vh built around one 3D model (a product or object, about 70vh tall, centred) on a flat ground. First 40% of the scroll: a 64px headline of two or three lines on the left over the model plus a 20px sub; at 40% the text fades out over 300px of scroll and the model takes over. The visitor can then orbit it with a pointer drag (damped 0.08, vertical angle clamped to 20 degrees) or the arrow keys, and 4 to 6 hotspots (solid accent discs 28px, still, projected from fixed points on the model) can be clicked. A click eases the camera to a preset view in 0.9s and opens a filled card beside the disc (tint fill, radius 16px, 320px wide, 24px padding, title 22px, two lines of 16px text); no leader lines. Colour roles: ground = ink or paper, discs = accent, cards = tint.
phone: Orbit by one-finger drag inside the stage only after the first tap on the model (otherwise the page scrolls), or a previous/next pill pair stepping camera presets; hotspots become 44px tap targets; the card docks at the bottom as a sheet with 20px gutters.
houseRuleCheck: The drag here is a 3D orbit, not a rail. No leader lines (hairlines); cards are fills; the headline fades before the model becomes interactive, so text never sits over boxes.

name: Idle float loop
description: One object (a product model, a set of three to five flat cards, a cut-out) hangs in the middle of a section and never stops moving: a vertical bob of about 10px on a 4-6s sine (ease-in-out), a slower sideways drift of 6px on a 7s sine and a rotation of +-2 degrees; with a set, every card has its own phase so the set ripples in depth. In WebGL it is the mesh transform; in the DOM a CSS keyframe on transform with will-change. The loop pauses when off screen and under reduced motion. No shadow under or behind the object at rest. Phone: the same with 30 percent less amplitude.
phone: Same, 30 percent less amplitude.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No shadow at rest, no drawn shapes; the motion is slow and never jerky.

name: Intro camera pullback
description: On load the 3D camera starts close (a macro of one object, or inside a tunnel of ribbons) and dollies back along its axis over 1-3s (power1 in-out; for example camera distance growing about 20 percent, say 21 to 25.5 in scene measure, at a 25 degree field of view) to a wide composition where the whole set reads. Props or picture planes rush past the lens in the first 40 percent. The hero headline (h1 step, 2-5 words), the navigation and the one action are HTML over the canvas and readable from the first frame; the camera move happens behind them. The camera then holds with a +-1 degree idle sway. The first screen is the canvas and the headline alone. Any input skips to the end in 300ms. Phone: 1.2s, lower resolution, same end frame.
phone: 1.2s, lower resolution, same end frame.
houseRuleCheck: Clean when the headline is there from the first frame: the camera move never holds the words back; skippable, under 3s, ending on a full-screen hero alone.

name: Models drop in spinning
description: On load three to five solid product models (each about 22% of the stage height) fall from above (or rise from below) into a fixed stage while spinning 360-720 degrees and growing from 0.4 to 1.0 scale over 1.6-3.2s (power4 in-out), then fan out into a row with 60-100px gaps and settle. The camera is still. The first screen is the stage: a 96-160px headline sits behind the models (overlapped by at most 15%) with one filled pill beneath. After the intro the models idle with a 4px bob and lift 3-4% on hover. Colour roles: flat brand ground, ink, the models bring the colours, accent on the button.
phone: The row becomes a 2 plus 1 arrangement at 60% size and the intro runs 1.6s; with reduced motion place the models in the final state.
houseRuleCheck: No cast shadows or glow; the headline stays readable; the intro ends before 3.2s and never gates the page.

name: Cut-out layers fly forward
description: An opening on load of about 2.2s. Ink or paper ground with a CSS 3D stage (perspective 1200px) or a WebGL scene. 12 to 16 flat cut-outs (transparent PNGs of products, objects or portraits, 200 to 520px) start far back (translateZ -1800 to -600, scaled down, opacity 0) and fly forward to resting depths between 0 and -400 in a 60ms stagger, 1.8s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), settling into a deep collage whose centre 640x360 stays free. The title (display 140px, one or two words) sits centred in that gap and is readable at once: its letters grow from the baseline (scaleY 0 to 1, origin bottom, 30ms apart, 0.6s) from the first frame and are done by 0.9s. After the intro the planes shift with the pointer by depth (translate = depth factor x pointer x 20px, eased 0.06). Colour roles: ground flat; the cut-outs carry all other colour; ink for the title. Variant: the pictures start as one fanned stack in an S-shaped ribbon across the screen and burst outward to scattered depths (scale 0.6-1.6, rotation up to 25 degrees, 8ms apart over 1.6s, power3 out), leaving the same clear centre for the title; once landed they never re-form.
phone: 8 planes at 120 to 260px; no pointer parallax (a slow 10s sway of 8px instead); title 72px.
houseRuleCheck: Layers are cut-out photographs or generated imagery, never sketches or drawn illustrations. No boxes on the pictures; the title is readable within a second; the hero still fills the first screen alone.

name: Scroll-posed 3D model
description: A sticky stage of 100svh inside 250-400vh of scroll holds one live 3D model (a product, a device, a vessel, a figure; 20-80k triangles, flat-lit) centred at about 55% of the stage height. Its pose is a function of scroll progress through a 0.08 lerp: yaw 0 to 360 degrees, a lid opening 0 to 90, an exploded view separating parts by up to 120px. Three or four short beats (40-64px, up to 10 words) alternate left and right of the model at about 14% and 62% of the width, in and out with progress. Colour roles: a flat ground tone chosen as the model's complement, ink contrasting, accent = one part of the model plus the closing button.
phone: Model at 55% height at the top with the beats beneath at 28-36px; pin 200vh, pixel ratio 1.5; with reduced motion show one static pose and the beats as plain blocks.
houseRuleCheck: No cast shadow, glow rim or gradient backdrop; the ground is flat and the model carries no text box.

name: Particle shape morph
description: A point cloud of 8,000-40,000 round points (2-3px) fills a fixed canvas stage (100svh), the points in the ink on the ground (or ground on ink) with one accent for a single chapter. Per scroll chapter (four or five chapters of one viewport each) the cloud morphs between forms sampled once in a worker from the page's own content: a word, the product's silhouette, the light and dark of a picture, never an abstract sphere or ring. Each morph takes 1.2-1.8s (power2 in-out) with each point on a curved path, 0-300ms of random delay and a scale of 1 to 1.4 midway. An h2-step headline and one caption of at most 15 words sit at the left in HTML. The first state may assemble from scattered segments and ends with a 300ms lift in brightness, not a white flash. Phone: 6,000-12,000 points, portrait framing, cloud 70 percent of the width.
phone: 6,000-12,000 points, portrait framing.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The points are rendered dots, not drawn line art or an illustration; no white full-screen flash; chapters are not numbered and no progress rail shows them.

name: Scroll relight
description: A pinned 3D scene of about 1800px of scroll with the camera fixed. One object (a device, case, chair or bottle, about 60vh tall) stands on a flat ground plane. A single time-of-day value is scrubbed 0 to 1 over the first 900px: the key light turns from warm white through amber to a deep blue grey, the ground tone goes from light to dark, the object's materials re-tint (a grey body goes blue) and any emissive part (a screen or lamp) brightens from 0.2 to 1; the cast shadow rotates about 60 degrees and lengthens about 2.4 times. Two captions (32px, two lines each, at the left, x 96) swap at 33% and 66% with a 400ms fade-rise. The geometry never moves. Colour roles: light and ground carry the colour change, accent = the emissive part.
phone: Same scene with a 1024 shadow map; captions below the stage in a filled card; range 1400px.
houseRuleCheck: The rendered shadow is scene lighting, not a UI drop shadow: every caption and card stays flat. The ground changes by flat tone, not by a page gradient.

name: Velocity-driven spin
description: A 3D object (a ring of 12-24 picture sprites, a bottle, a coin, a sculpture) idles at 0.1-0.25 rad per second. Scroll speed adds angular velocity (velocity x 0.0006 rad per px/s, capped at 3x idle) in the direction of scroll and eases back to idle with damping 0.94 per frame. Optionally the pointer drags it with inertia. It sits in a hero or a 150vh section at 55-65% of the viewport height with a 96-160px headline behind it. Colour roles: flat ground, the object brings the colour, ink contrasting, accent on the button.
phone: Pixel ratio 1.5 and 40% of the sprites; touch swipes add velocity; with reduced motion no spin.
houseRuleCheck: Sprites are photographs or cut-outs, not drawn shapes; no glow and no shadow.

name: Tiles snap together
description: 24-80 3D tiles or blocks (flat planes or boxes, each a flat palette colour or a slice of a picture) fly into one form: the picture they were cut from, the product's own shape, or a wall or stack of them. Each tile starts a few tile-widths out with a random rotation and rises into place over 700ms (power3 out), top tiles first with a 20-40ms stagger downward. It assembles once, scrubbed over one viewport of scroll as the section arrives, and comes apart only in reverse; a timed version plays once on entry over about 1.6s and holds. The camera sits still or sways +-1 degree. Colours by role: tiles in ink and accent on the ground. Phone: 24 tiles.
phone: 24 tiles, same assembly.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Tiles are flat colours or picture slices, never drawn illustration, with no outlines; no endless explode-and-reassemble loop.

name: Surface cracks apart
description: A pinned scene of about 2400px, scrubbed. One large picture (2:1, 1200x600, centred) is cut into 40 to 70 irregular tiles along baked crack lines (a Voronoi cut in the mesh), all textured from the same picture so at rest it looks whole. From progress 0.15 the tiles break from a crack origin outward in order: each shrinks to 0.85, tilts up to 12 degrees on two axes and drifts away from the centre by 0 to 3 tile widths, staggered by distance from the origin, revealing the ink ground between. The camera dollies forward along a short path (z 8 to 4) with a 3-degree roll. At 60% a headline (80px, two lines) appears in the opened gap; the section releases at the end. Colour roles: ground = ink; the picture supplies the colour; headline = paper.
phone: 24 tiles; picture full width minus 40px; range 1800px; headline below the stage.
houseRuleCheck: Cracks are gaps that show the ground, not drawn lines (no hairlines); no outlines on tiles.

name: Labels pinned to 3D
description: A pinned 3D scene (a globe, a ring of crystals; 2-4 viewport heights of scroll) moves with scroll while 4-12 HTML labels track points on it. Every frame each label's screen position is projected from its 3D anchor, so a label can travel up to 1800px across the viewport, staggered, as the object turns; it fades from 0.4 to 1 as its anchor faces the camera and to 0 behind it. A label is a solid pill 36px tall at 16px sentence case, 1-3 words, ground on ink or ink on accent, attached to its anchor by a 10px accent dot with the pill 14px to its right (flipping left near the edge); there is no leader line. Phone: five labels at most, 32px pills, only anchors near the middle.
phone: Five labels at most, 32px pills, near-centre anchors only.
houseRuleCheck: Clean with a dot and a solid pill in place of leader lines (hairline rules), and no faint ghost words behind the scene. Labels are sentence case at 16px, not tiny uppercase.

name: Poster wall rush-in
description: An arrival move after a click or on load. A vertical wheel of 40 to 60 poster cells (3 columns of posters 360x480 with 24px gaps; designed 3:4 posters or product art) begins offset by 60 cells and glides in over 2.4s with exponential ease-out; poster blur is proportional to travel speed (a directional blur up to 14px in a shader, or a CSS blur stepped by velocity), so the posters rush in blurred and sharpen only at the end. After landing the column rests on the poster at the centre (scale 1, neighbours 0.9) and the page ground stays flat. One 56px filled pill (the click that triggered it) is the only control. One shot per session. Colour roles: ground = ink or paper, the posters carry all other colour.
phone: 2 columns, posters 160x220 with 12px gaps; 1.8s; blur capped at 8px.
houseRuleCheck: No drag: after the arrival the wall moves by scroll only. Nothing sits on the posters.

name: Camera steps between rooms
description: A pinned 3D scene in one canvas holds four to seven named stops (rooms, floors, camera positions). The stage is held for about one screen of scroll per stop: when the scroll crosses a stop's threshold the camera tweens to it in 1s (in-out cubic) as a timed move, and the arrow keys or a click on a hotspot do the same; the wheel is never captured and the page keeps its native scroll. At each stop a caption block fades in at the left after 600ms (h2 of 2-4 words and one 18px line) while the previous one leaves in 200ms. Hotspots are 44px filled discs in the accent that show one word on hover. After the last stop the stage releases and the page scrolls on. A visible Next text button is the fallback for keyboard and mouse. Phone: vertical swipe, 48px hotspots.
phone: Native scroll steps it, 48px hotspots, visible Next button.
houseRuleCheck: Clean on native scroll: no wheel capture, no stop counter, no dot rail for the stops; the stage releases after the last stop.

name: Arrow-stepped card row
description: A row of three or four filled cards (each 400-420px wide by 520px high at 1440, 24px gap, radius 0-20px, fill = tone stepped from the ground; a 4:3 picture on top, a 24px title and a 17px two-line text) is clipped at the container's edges, so the next card peeks about 80px inside the container. Two filled circular buttons (56px, ink fill, ground-colour arrow glyph) sit top-right beside the 48px section heading on the left. A click advances one card (width plus gap) over 600-700ms on the house curve; at either end the button drops to 30% opacity. Keyboard arrows work. Colour roles: ground flat, card fill, ink, accent only on the closing link.
phone: A native snap row with cards at 82vw so the next peeks 8vw, arrows hidden, 16-20px gutters.
houseRuleCheck: An index counter beside the arrows is the usual extra: dropped. Arrows are filled circles, not outlined; no drag cue; the row clips at the container, not at one screen edge.

name: Hero product switcher
description: A hero (100svh) shows exactly one product at the centre (a cut-out picture or a 3D model, 520-640px tall) on a flat ground that is that product's own colour. Two 56px filled discs at the left and right edges, 40px in, plus the arrow keys (and a swipe on touch), swap to the next of four to six variants: the old product slides out by 24 percent of its width and fades in 300ms while the new one enters from the other side, 80px offset, in 700ms (expo-out); the ground cross-fades to the new product's colour in 600ms; the name (h2 step, 1-3 words) and one 18px line roll in through a mask in 400ms; the button stays. There is no autoplay. Phone: product 60 percent of the width, swipe plus two arrow discs at the bottom corners.
phone: Product 60 percent wide, swipe plus two arrow discs at the bottom corners.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Ground swaps are flat colours, never gradients; no dots or counters; arrows are filled discs, not outlined. It steps by its arrows, keys or a swipe on touch, never a mouse drag.

name: Timer-fill autoplay
description: A split section. At the left a stack of three to five selector cards, each 520 x 112px with a 20px radius, an h4-step title and one 16px line on a ground-tint fill; at the right a picture window 640-760 x 520px with a 24px radius. The active card fills like a timer: its own face fills with the accent from the bottom to the top (translateY 100 percent to 0, linear over 8-12s), the text switching to the ground colour once the fill passes it; there is no separate bar or line. When it is full the card scales 1 to 0.95 and returns to its idle fill (600ms), the next card starts to fill, outgoing text leaves upward 150 percent through a mask, and the picture window dips to the ground colour for 120ms and swaps to the next picture (scale 1.2 to 1 in 800ms, expo-out). A click on a card jumps to it and restarts; hover, focus and leaving the viewport pause it, and under reduced motion nothing advances on its own. Phone: the cards become a row of three compact pills 220 x 88px above the window; the fill works the same.
phone: Three compact pills above the picture window, same face-fill timer.
houseRuleCheck: The timer is the card's own face filling, so there is no bar, no thin line and no numbering; it is a card state, not a scroll-progress bar. Autoplay pauses on hover, focus and off screen and is off under reduced motion. Cards are filled, not outlined.

name: Vertical wrap wheel
description: A pinned stage of about 600vh whose scroll position moves a vertical column of 8 to 12 poster cells that wraps endlessly in Y. Cells are 520x680 with a 24px gap, centred at x 900 (right of centre); the active cell at scale 1, the neighbours above and below at 0.82 and 50% opacity. Scroll maps to column offset with lerp 0.05; 140ms after input stops the column settles onto the nearest whole cell (ease-out 500ms); the arrow keys step one cell. At the left a caption block (title 48px, two lines of 18px text, one text link) swaps with a mask roll when the active cell changes (24px rise, 300ms). There is no drag handler on mouse or touch: scroll or keys only, so there is no rail to drag. Colour roles: ground = ink or paper; the posters carry the colour; accent = the link.
phone: Column centred at about 72% of the width, cells 260x360, caption under the stage in a filled card; scroll maps the same way.
houseRuleCheck: Scroll and keys move the column and nothing is dragged, so it is no drag rail; the wheel is never captured (scroll position drives a held stage that releases at its end); endless wrapping leaves no empty end.

name: Click image burst
description: A small click reaction on a word or button (a chapter name, a category, a primary action). On click 8 to 12 round-cropped images (48 to 72px, cut from the page's own pictures, never plain tint discs) burst from the click point in a 120-degree upward arc, travelling 50 to 100px (randomised) while scaling 0.3 to 1.2 over 0.9s power2.out and fading out after 0.4s; the elements are pooled and removed on finish. The clicked word dips 4% and returns in 200ms. Colour roles: the images carry the colour; ground and ink unchanged; no accent. Under reduced motion skip the burst and keep the dip.
phone: 6 to 8 particles at 40 to 56px; fires on tap; no hover state.
houseRuleCheck: Images only, never emoji glyphs; no outlines on the discs.

name: Card widens on select
description: A row of 4 to 5 selectable cards in a 1312px container (64px side margins), 560px high, 16px gaps, radius 20px, tint fills. The selected card takes 42% of the row (about 540px) and its picture fills it, fading in and scaling 1.2 to 1 over 700ms; the others share the rest equally (about 170px each) and show only a tinted fill with their title at the top in 20px, two lines. Select by click or tap on a card, by filled chips above the row or by two 56px circle arrows; widths animate with cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) over 700ms; the active card's text (title 28px, two lines of 16px, one pill) rises 24px and fades in after 300ms. Colour roles: tints from one hue family, accent for the active pill, ink for text.
phone: Vertical accordion: cards stacked with 12px gaps; the selected one grows from 96px to 420px tall with the same photo fade; tap selects; one open at a time.
houseRuleCheck: Cards are fills (wanted); no drag and no rail. Text laid directly on the picture needs a flat ink layer, never a gradient or a box; all gaps are real space and nothing touches the edge.

name: Liquid pour on press
description: A product action that triggers a 3s liquid render. A product cut-out (a can, bottle or jar, about 560px tall) stands centred; at its opening sits a 56px filled round button. A press starts a WebGL fluid pour (a small stable-fluid solver on a 256x256 grid, splats from the opening) in one flat accent colour with a simple specular and no transparency; the pour fills the screen from the bottom in 1.6s. The liquid texture is then reused as the transition mask: the next section is revealed wherever the liquid has been, over 1.2s. Optional sound on press, off until the visitor has enabled sound. Colour roles: ground = ink or paper, liquid = accent, the product carries its own colours.
phone: Without a fast GPU use a flat accent clip-path rise from the bottom (1.2s); fluid only on devices that hold 60fps in a short benchmark.
houseRuleCheck: The liquid is a flat accent colour, not glassy or gradient-shaded. The trigger is a press on a button, not a drag; no sound without consent.

name: Scan beam shrink
description: A product-card reaction to a primary action. The card: a product picture on a tint fill (radius 20px, 420x520) with a filled pill (56px high) under it. On press a 14px solid dot at the button stretches into a 324x6 flat bar in the accent colour (500ms power2.out); the bar travels from the top of the picture to the bottom in 600ms with no glow and no sound; then the product picture scales from 1 to 0 toward the bag target in 180ms (power4.inOut) while the card keeps its fill. The pill label turns into a sentence-case confirmation and the card tone shifts one step. A plain 'Undo' text link reverses it within 2s. Colour roles: card tint = ground, bar = accent, ink for labels.
phone: Bar spans the picture's full width; same timing; the bag target is the bag button in the bottom tab bar.
houseRuleCheck: The bar is a flat 6px fill (not a hairline) with no glow and no beep; it starts from a solid dot, not a ring (no outlines); the bag target is a plain filled dot, no counter.

name: Click theme switch
description: A product or character hero with a theme switch. Three colourways of the same subject (three pictures or textures of identical framing) and three themes, each a ground, an ink and one accent. A row of three filled swatches (44px circles, 12px apart, bottom left of the hero at a 48px margin; the active one scales to 1.2) or the arrow keys switches theme. Over 700ms the hero picture crossfades to the new colourway (a plain crossfade, never a hue rotation that sweeps through other colours), the section grounds change colour through CSS variables and cards and tiles retint to the new accent tone. Only one theme is on screen at a time; the swatches are the only place the others appear. Remember the choice in localStorage.
phone: Swatches 40px in a row above the safe area, centred; transitions 500ms.
houseRuleCheck: Three themes exist but one shows at a time (no colour sprawl); none is violet or lavender; swatches are filled circles with no rings.

name: Elliptical visor wipe
description: A scrubbed colour turn between two sections over 720px of scroll. A layer in the next section's ground (for example ink) is clipped by clip-path ellipse(70% 0% at 50% 0%) and grows to ellipse(70% 100% at 50% 0%) as scroll runs, so a curved lower edge sags down the screen like a visor and ends as full cover. The content inside the layer (a headline 72px, centred, in the opposite ink) sits in the lower third and rises 40px as the visor passes. Reverse the colours for a light reveal over a dark section. Built with a sticky layer and one CSS variable for the radius: no gradient, no blur. Colour roles: ground A and ground B (one is ink), ink flips, accent none.
phone: Ellipse 120% wide; range 540px.
houseRuleCheck: The edge is a hard clip with no gradient and no outline.

name: Ground retones per section
description: A fixed page ground variable and the navigation ink switch to the colour of the section entering the middle line of the viewport, either by a 400ms fade on the house curve or by a hard cut. Each section declares a ground and an ink; three to five tones from one palette (a cream, a near-black, one saturated ground, a soft stone), and the section backgrounds themselves are transparent so the page colour shows through. The barless navigation changes ink at the same instant. Text contrast stays 7:1 or better in every state. Colour roles: three to five grounds from one palette, one pair of inks, accent used on only one ground.
phone: Same trigger with the threshold at 55%; with reduced motion use hard cuts.
houseRuleCheck: At most four grounds from one brand palette (no colour sprawl), no violet or lavender, flat colours only, never a gradient.

name: Scrubbed ground fade
description: The page ground is a variable blended continuously with scroll between section tones: each section declares a tone, and between its midpoint and the next one's midpoint the ground interpolates in OKLCH over 60-100vh of scroll, so the page breathes from a warm grey to near-black, or from cream to a saturated tone. Ink for text and navigation swaps at the 50% point of each blend. Inside any section there is no gradient: at every moment the whole page is one flat colour. Optionally a fixed multiply layer over the photographs lets them pick up the ground tint. Three or four tones only. Colour roles: ground (moving), two inks, accent on one ground.
phone: Identical; with reduced motion switch the ground in hard steps at the midpoints.
houseRuleCheck: A white-to-lilac blend is the usual form: lilac and violet are banned, so tones come from the page palette; the page is one flat colour at any instant, so it is not a gradient; four tones at most.

name: Colour block slides up
description: The next section's flat ground rides up over the current one with a visible straight edge: a full-width sheet (min-height 100vh, radius 0) slides over at normal speed, or is scrubbed from translateY(100%) to 0 over 100vh while the section beneath stays pinned. The outgoing section's heading or scene tints with the sweep: a clip-path mask on a second copy of the text swaps the ink at the edge's position, so letters change colour exactly as the edge passes them. Hard edge, no gradient, no shadow. Three or four flat grounds from one palette. Colour roles: flat grounds, two inks, accent on one sheet.
phone: The same sweep over 90vh; with reduced motion plain stacked sections.
houseRuleCheck: The edge is a straight flat colour change with no shadow and no gradient; at most four colours, no violet.

name: Active title brightens
description: The state style for any list that drives a stepped or pinned scene. A list of 3 to 6 step titles (words, 24 to 32px, in the display or text face) stacked at the left edge of the scene at x 64, 16px apart, or set in a row at the top. Inactive titles sit at 40% ink opacity; the title of the current step goes to 100% over 100ms ease-in (and back over 200ms). Optional: the active title gets a filled tint chip behind it that fades in, never an underline. Nothing counts or moves; clicking a title jumps to its step. Colour roles: ink on ground; accent only for the optional chip.
phone: The titles wrap onto two lines of filled chips under the stage (44px high), the active chip at full ink.
houseRuleCheck: Step titles (words) carry the state, never numerals, so it is an opacity switch with no index or counter; inactive titles stay at 40%, still readable.

name: Stat count-up
description: Figures in a stat card interpolate from 0 (or from 60-90% of the final value) up to the final value over 1.2-1.8s, ease-out-cubic, once, when the card crosses 70% of the viewport. The numeral is 72-140px at 1440 in tabular figures, the headline face at tracking -0.02em, with its unit and a 17px one-line meaning beneath. Three or four filled cards in a row (300-420px wide, 280-340px high, radius 0-20px, fill a tone stepped from the ground, content left aligned and anchored to the bottom), or one big figure per section. Cards stagger by 120ms. The true final text is in the markup from the start. Colour roles: flat ground, card fill, ink, accent on a single unit.
phone: Cards one or two across, numerals 56-72px; with reduced motion show the final values at once.
houseRuleCheck: Figures must be real facts with a unit and a meaning, never an index such as 01 or 02; cards carry no icon above them and no outline; the cards must not be the only element on the page.

name: Odometer digit roll
description: A real figure (a year, a price, a distance, a measure of 2-4 digits) at the h1 or h2 step (96-200px) in the tabular figures of the page's proportional display face is built from one column per digit. Each column is a clipped window exactly one digit tall (line height 1, overflow hidden) holding the digits 0-9 stacked. On trigger (the section 60 percent in view, or a scroll step in a pinned timeline) each column rolls up by whole rows (28-112px, one row per step) to its target digit in 1s with expo-out, columns staggered 80ms from the last digit to the first. In a timeline variant the year rolls to its next value every 400-600px of scroll while a one-line caption swaps with a mask roll. Ink on ground; no accent. Phone: the figure at 72-96px, same roll.
phone: Figure at 72-96px, same roll.
houseRuleCheck: Clean if used for a real figure; it must never be a 01/02/03 section number or a slide counter, and the digits are tabular figures of the proportional face, not a monospace one. No fill bar beside it.

name: Camera looks with pointer
description: A 3D scene (a room, a shelf of products, an interior, a landscape) whose camera rotates toward or against the pointer: yaw up to 6 degrees and pitch up to 4 degrees (or a sideways offset of 0.3 metres of scene space) with damping lerp 0.08 (floaty) to 0.12 (snappy), returning to centre when the pointer leaves. The scene is the backdrop of a full-screen hero; the hero text is DOM and stays still, or moves at 0.3 of the camera's parallax for depth. Colour roles: ground = the scene's tone, ink contrasting, accent on the button.
phone: No pointer, so a gentle auto-sway of 2 degrees on a 10s sine, or device tilt at 3 degrees; with reduced motion a still.
houseRuleCheck: Flat light and fog, no glow and no gradient sky.

name: Depth-map pointer parallax
description: A full-bleed hero or scene block where a flat picture gains depth from the pointer. Assets: the picture (3:2 or 16:10, cover fit) and a same-size greyscale depth map (white near, black far; produced by a depth-estimation tool, painted by hand, or faked from three cut-out layers). A fixed-canvas fragment shader samples the colour at uv + (depth - 0.5) x pointer x 0.05, where pointer runs -1 to 1 and is eased with lerp 0.06, so near parts shift up to about 36px at 1440 and far parts the opposite way; scale the picture 1.06 to hide edge stretch. The headline (display 120px, two lines) stays in the DOM above and never moves. Colour roles: the picture; ink = white on dark pictures; accent = the button only. Without WebGL, stack three cut-out layers translated by 12, 24 and 36px instead.
phone: Pointer replaced by a looping drift (8s Lissajous, amplitude 14px) or device tilt where permitted; picture cropped to 100svh.
houseRuleCheck: Use a designed, generated or product picture, never a documentary photograph; no text boxes on it.

name: Pointer fluid smear
description: A full-viewport WebGL layer runs a fluid simulation (velocity, pressure, curl, dissipation 0.97-0.985, splat radius 0.2-0.35% of the width) in which pointer speed adds velocity and dye. The dye advects and fades in 1.5-3s, smearing the scene beneath: either a fog of two palette colours over a dark ground, or a displacement of the hero image or headline texture. Dye is limited to two palette tones plus ink, with no colour cycling. The hero headline stays a DOM element at 96-160px with the dye blended over it by a difference or multiply layer. When idle an automatic splat every 4s keeps the scene alive. Colour roles: ground = a flat tone, dye = accent and a second palette tone.
phone: Touch traces act as the pointer, simulation at 128 resolution, idle splats every 3s; with reduced motion show a still of a smeared frame.
houseRuleCheck: Fluid defaults cycle rainbow colours and blend as gradients: dye is limited to two palette tones, never violet; pair only with a calm hero because it is heavy, and keep the text legible.

name: Pointer image trail
description: On a clean flat ground the pointer leaves pictures behind it. Each time the pointer has travelled about one sixteenth of the viewport width (90px at 1440) a new picture is placed centred on it: 150-240px on its long side, 6-10px radius, a random tilt of up to 6 degrees, taken in turn from a set of 8-12 pictures. A picture starts at 0.8 scale and 0 opacity and reaches 1 in 200ms (expo-out) and stays while the pointer moves; once the pointer has rested 350ms the pictures leave one by one, oldest first, shrinking to 0.2 and fading over 0.8-1.2s. No more than 10 are alive at once and the newest is always on top. The native cursor stays. A headline at the h1 step (2-4 words, ink) sits centred and the pictures pass under it so it stays readable. Pictures are cut-out objects, textures or designed stills, never documentary photographs; ground and ink are flat, the accent is used only on the one action. Phone: no pointer, so a tap drops the next picture at the finger (100px), six alive at most, each fading after 1.2s.
phone: No pointer: a tap drops a 100px picture at the finger, six alive at most.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The pictures must be designed stills or cut-outs, not documentary photographs; they pass under the headline so no box ever sits on a photograph and none carries a caption.

name: Pill label follows cursor
description: A solid pill 32px tall with 14px side padding, filled in the accent with ground-coloured letters at 16px medium, follows the pointer about 16px to its right and below it, eased with a 0.12 lerp so it trails by a few frames. It holds one or two words in sentence case that name what a click does (Open, Play, Read the story) and it only exists over targets (picture cards, tiles, list rows). On entering a target it grows from 0.7 scale and 0 opacity to 1 in 300ms on the house curve, with no overshoot, while the native pointer stays visible beside it; on leaving it shrinks back in 200ms. Within 140px of the right or bottom edge it flips to the left or above the pointer so it never leaves the viewport. When the pointer moves from one target type to another the words change by a short mask roll (180ms). Ground and ink are the page's own; only the pill takes the accent. Phone: no cursor, so each target carries its own visible action button instead.
phone: No cursor; every target shows its own visible action button.
houseRuleCheck: A companion label, not a cursor: the system pointer always stays and nothing overshoots. A filled pill, not an outline; one or two words in sentence case at 16px, so it is not a caption box on a photograph. Hidden on touch, where each target shows its own action.

name: Pointer lens warp
description: A pointer lens on a full-bleed picture or scene. A post pass (or a shader on the media plane) bulges the image inside a 180px radius (at 1440) around the eased pointer (lerp 0.1): the uv is pushed away from the pointer by 0.18 x (1 - smoothstep(0, radius, distance)), which magnifies the centre smoothly with no colour fringe. The lens grows from 0 to full radius in 400ms on entering the block and back in 400ms on leaving. The lens is invisible as a shape: no rim, no highlight. The headline stays in the DOM above. Colour roles: the media only.
phone: A touch-drag moves the lens; at rest an auto path across the picture every 8s; radius 120px.
houseRuleCheck: No rim or glass highlight: the lens is a pure distortion, not a glass object.

name: Paint trail reveal
description: A pointer-painted reveal on a large picture. Two treatments of the same image are stacked in a canvas: a base (full colour, or a flat ink duotone) and an alternate (a pale paper tone with a halftone dot pattern, cell 16px, dot size from luminance). The pointer paints a brush (radius 0.04 of the canvas width) into a 512x512 offscreen buffer that fades x0.97 per frame, so the trail shows about 2s of path. The mix between the treatments follows the buffer: the picture turns pale and halftoned where the pointer has passed and heals as the trail decays. Block 1360x700 with 40px margins and radius 24, or a full-bleed hero; a 96px headline sits on the plain ground above or beside it, not on the picture. Colour roles: ground = paper, ink = near black, no accent.
phone: A touch-drag paints; on load a self-moving brush traces an S across the picture for 2s to show it works.
houseRuleCheck: Halftone is a texture of dots, not a drawn illustration; text stays off the picture.

name: Hover preview follows
description: A list of 5-12 rows, each with a name at the h2 step (56-96px) starting at the left margin and a short descriptor aligned right at 18px, rows 120-160px tall on the ground, no divider rules (separation by space and by the row's own fill on hover). Hovering a row fades in a preview picture 280-320px wide (4:5 or 3:2, 8-12px radius) over 0.5s (power2-out) which follows the pointer with a spring (stiffness about 170, damping 26, or a 0.12 lerp), offset 24px to its right and tilting up to 4 degrees with pointer speed. The row inverts to an ink band with ground letters in 180ms; the other rows stay. Leaving fades the preview out in 0.5s. One picture per row. Phone: no hover, so a tap opens the row as an accordion with its picture at full width, 4:3, one open at a time.
phone: Tap opens the row as an accordion with a full-width 4:3 picture.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No hairline dividers between rows; the inverted band is the row's own fill; names start at the left margin so rows are not empty on the left; the preview is a picture with no box on a photograph.

name: Pointer repel field
description: A stage 100svh tall on a flat ground holds 12-40 tiles (picture tiles 120-200px, picture discs, or short words at 48px) scattered in a loose grid with 8-20 percent jitter. A pointer within 220px of a tile pushes it away along the line from the pointer (force falling off with the square of the distance, up to 90px) and rotates it up to 15 degrees; pointer speed scales the push. When the pointer leaves, each tile eases home by 5 percent of its remaining offset per frame, about 600ms. A headline at the h1 step (2-4 words) sits centred above the tiles in z-order. There is no fluid trail. Phone: no pointer, so tiles drift away from a touch while the finger is down and otherwise float 6px on a slow sine.
phone: Tiles drift away from a held touch, otherwise float 6px.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Tiles are pictures or words; no decorative drawn discs; the headline is plain type without a box.

name: Pointer lights the text
description: A statement block where the pointer lights the words. A statement of 12 to 20 words, 36 to 48px, up to 5 lines, 900px wide at most, each word in its own span. At rest every word sits at 45% ink opacity, already readable. As the pointer moves each word's opacity eases (120ms) to 45% + 55% x (1 - clamp(distance / 220px)), distance taken from the pointer to the word's centre, so words near the pointer read at full ink while the rest stay dimmer; leaving the block returns all to 45% in 500ms. There is no lamp, glow or light shape: only the words change. On a dark ground the ink is paper white. Colour roles: ground flat, ink; accent none.
phone: No pointer: the words light by distance from a line at 45% of the viewport height as the block scrolls through it, so reading order follows the scroll.
houseRuleCheck: No lamp shape: a soft radial lamp would be a gradient, so per-word opacity does the lighting, with no glow; the dim words never drop below 45%.

name: Tilt toward pointer
description: A card, title block, disc or 3D model rotates in perspective (perspective 900-1200px) toward the pointer: rotateX and rotateY up to 6-10 degrees at a strength of about 0.2 of the normalised pointer offset, returning on leave by a critically damped spring (stiffness 170, damping 26, no overshoot) or a 500ms ease-out. For a card 360-480px wide the picture inside counter-translates 8-14px for depth. No shine overlay and no shadow. For a 3D model the model's rotation follows the pointer instead of the DOM. Use it on one to three key objects per page, not on every card. Colour roles: none.
phone: Not on touch; device orientation at 4 degrees is optional and off by default; with reduced motion none.
houseRuleCheck: No glare or shine gradient and no moving shadow: the rotation alone carries it.

name: Flat colour wash interlude
description: A 720px colour pause between two scenes of a scrolled story (3D, photo or pinned text scenes). A fixed full-viewport layer in one flat accent colour (a warm or cool hue, never violet or lavender) fades in over 120px of scroll (opacity 0 to 1), holds for 360px, then fades out over 240px; the scene behind swaps at the middle of the hold, so the visitor sees a clean flat colour and then the next scene emerging from it. In the hold a single statement can sit centred (display 72px, up to 6 words, in the page ink or paper by contrast), rising 24px and fading in at 30% of the hold. Colour roles: wash = accent, ink by contrast.
phone: Same sequence over 540px in total; statement 44px.
houseRuleCheck: The wash is the page's single accent, never violet or lavender; the 'mist' is an opacity fade of a flat colour, never a gradient.

name: Glitch slice handover
description: A first-scroll handover on a hero portrait or object. The hero shows one cut-out or photograph plane (centred, about 620px tall) on a flat ground. On the first 400px of scroll (scrubbed, then it plays out in 900ms once triggered) the plane breaks into 10 to 16 horizontal slices (strips of the same texture, 40 to 62px high). The slices offset sideways by random distances (30 to 160px) with a 30ms stagger, then slide out left and right while the next section's ground wipes in. The rest state is clean. Colour roles: the picture carries the colour, ground flat, ink for text.
phone: 8 slices, offsets up to 60px; triggered by the first 200px of scroll.
houseRuleCheck: No wireframe of thin lines behind the portrait (no hairlines) and no flicker: the slices move once and leave. The hero still fills the first screen alone.

name: Glyph fragments flip in
description: A title build of about 1.1s on load or on entering view. Display title 120 to 160px, one or two lines. Each letter is cut into 3 or 4 horizontal strips (the DOM letter cloned once per strip and clipped with clip-path inset so each shows one band); the strips flip in from rotateX(90deg) to 0 (perspective 800px), the strips of one letter 20ms apart and letters 25ms apart, 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1). While flipping the strips are tinted with the accent, and the tint settles to the page ink over 400ms after the last strip lands, so at rest it is one plain word. Set aria-label on the parent. Colour roles: ink at rest, accent while flipping, ground flat.
phone: Title 56 to 72px, 2 strips per letter.
houseRuleCheck: A flat accent tint that fades to ink stands in for any bloom, so nothing glows and nothing is left at rest; the tint is transient, not a styled accent word.

name: Halftone shader treatment
description: A picture (or a warped colour field) is rendered by a fragment shader as a halftone in exactly two colours from the palette: ink dots on the ground, or ground dots on the accent. The grid has 4-8px cells at 45 degrees and the dot radius follows the picture's luminance; a scan-line variant uses 3px lines of varying thickness. The treatment is persistent on the hero or on one section picture. On press and hold the dots swell and go gooey (metaball blend 0.58, contrast 1.5, wave amplitude doubled) and relax over 600ms on release. The picture reveals with a uniform going 0 to 1 over 2s (cubic-bezier 0.31, 0.75, 0.22, 1). Type over it is HTML, crisp, in the colour with the better contrast. Phone: 6px cells, press effect by touch.
phone: 6px cells, press effect by touch.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Two flat colours, no smooth tones: the impression of tone comes from dot size, not from a gradient. No box over the picture.

name: Angled image wipe
description: A card or gallery image with two states: each image has an alternate picture (for example the product, then the same product in use). The image is a plane (WebGL shader) or two stacked images; a shader mixes the two textures through a wipe whose edge is angled at 30 degrees, progress 0 to 1 over 700ms cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) on hover (desktop) or when the card passes the middle of the viewport (touch). The picture also shifts by a parallax offset of up to 6% of its height with scroll and scales 1.04 on hover. CSS alternative: two stacked images, the top one clipped by clip-path polygon(0 0, X% 0, calc(X% - 12%) 100%, 0 100%) with X animated from 0 to 112. Cards 440x560, radius 16, tint fill, a 22px title and one line under the picture. Colour roles: card tint = ground, ink for text.
phone: The wipe plays once when the card is 60% in view; no hover state.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict: text sits in the card's own fill under the picture, never over it.

name: Zoomable flat map
description: A map block 1312x640 inside 64px margins (radius 24px, tint fill), a self-styled flat vector map in four colours: land = ground tone, water = a tint, roads = a slightly darker land tone (3px or wider), labels = ink (14 to 16px, sentence case). 8 to 12 pins are solid accent dots (14px) that open a filled card on hover or tap (tint fill, radius 16, 260px wide, a 20px title and one line of 16px text). Controls: two filled 48px circle buttons (zoom in and zoom out, glyphs from the typeface) at the lower right 24px in; wheel zoom only with ctrl or cmd held so the page still scrolls; a three-stop zoom stack (region, city, street) and an idle auto-fly between pins every 6s until the visitor touches the map. The data licence's one-line attribution sits in the corner at 12px. A pin card may grow from scale 0 to 1 at the pin point in 250ms on the house curve, never with an overshoot (a solid ink card 12px above the pin with a name and one short line at 16px), and shrink back in 200ms on leave.
phone: Block full width minus 40px, 70svh high; two-finger pan and zoom (one finger scrolls the page); pins open the card as a bottom sheet; buttons 44px.
houseRuleCheck: Pins are filled dots, not icons. The licence-required attribution is a single short line, not a credit wall. The map style has no gradient and no outlines.

name: Leaf shadow sway
description: A ground texture for one calm section (a quote, values or story block, 100vh). A fragment shader fills the section with dappled light and shadow: domain-warped noise thresholded with a smoothstep between 0.42 and 0.5 so the patches read as leaf-shaped shadows, in the ink colour at 8 to 12% opacity over a warm paper ground. The pattern sways on time (offset sin(t x 0.3) x 12px on a slow 20s drift) and is nudged by the pointer through a spring (stiffness 40, damping 8, up to 20px). The layer fades in as the section rises into view (opacity 0 to 1 over the first 400px) and moves up 77px against the page while the section passes. Text and cards above are flat and opaque, in front of the texture. Colour roles: ground = warm paper, shadow = ink at low opacity, accent none.
phone: The pointer is replaced by a 14s autonomous drift; half resolution; paused when off screen.
houseRuleCheck: The shadows are an ambient ground texture (a lit surface), not a UI drop shadow: every card and text block stays flat, and the patch edges stay moderately crisp, so there is no soft gradient glow.

name: Veil dissolves on load
description: A load-state cover over a 3D or media canvas. Until the model or media has loaded, a flat veil in the page ground colour covers the canvas. When loading finishes the veil does not fade as a sheet: it dissolves through an ordered 4x4 dither threshold in a fragment shader (or a canvas), cells of 4px dropping out in a noisy order across 1s (inOutCubic on the threshold), so the scene appears through shrinking dots of ground and then clears. The page's own first screen (headline, sentence, action) is HTML around the canvas and readable from the first frame; only the canvas waits. Colour roles: veil = page ground, scene = its own colours; no accent.
phone: Cells 6px, 0.8s, DPR 1.
houseRuleCheck: The veil is one flat ground colour dissolved by a dither threshold, never a gradient; it covers only the canvas, never the page's words, and it does not pulse.

name: Noise dissolve reveal
description: A one-shot reveal of a hero or a large media block. The media is drawn by a shader with a progress value 0 to 1 over 1.8s (cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)), triggered on load or when 40% in view. A 4D noise field (x, y, time and a fixed seed) is compared with the progress: pixels below the threshold show the media, pixels above show the ground. At the leading edge a band about 60px wide shows the media as halftone dots (cell 10px, dot radius shrinking toward the unrevealed side); behind the band a pale wash of the ground colour at 40% fades out; at 95% a soft brightness pulse (1.0 to 1.2 to 1.0 over 300ms, never a strobe) closes the reveal. Colour roles: ground = paper or ink, the media carries the colour.
phone: Same shader at DPR 1 over 1.4s; or a CSS mask-image with a bitmap noise PNG whose mask-position animates.
houseRuleCheck: The pulse is capped (no flashing) for photosensitivity. Halftone is a texture of dots, not a drawn illustration.

name: Drifting noise ground
description: A full-screen fragment shader (fractal noise, 4-5 octaves, flow speed 0.02-0.05 of the noise scale per second) drifts slowly behind the content as smoke or cloud sheets in two or three palette tones. It is posterised into 4-6 flat bands with crisp edges (smoothstep width 0.01), so it reads as layered paper or a contour map rather than a soft glow. The headline is DOM text on top at 96-180px. The ground can darken per chapter: a depth value eases 0 to 1 over 1.2s when a new section enters. Render at 50% resolution and upscale; pause when hidden; a static frame under reduced motion and data saver. Colour roles: ground = the darkest band, two lighter palette tones, ink contrasting, accent on the button.
phone: Resolution 35%, speed halved; with reduced motion one still frame.
houseRuleCheck: It often adds faint arcs and ramp discs: dropped as drawn shapes. Smooth blends read as gradients, so the noise is quantised to flat colour bands.

name: Velocity bend
description: Images are WebGL planes aligned with their DOM boxes (4:5, 380x475, in a 3-4 column gallery or a vertical list). A shader offsets the vertices by scroll velocity: planes bend (a sine curve up to 40px at top speed) and may blur up to 2px, relaxing by a 0.08 lerp to flat within 400ms when scrolling stops. Scroll is smoothed (lerp 0.1) so velocity is continuous. Planes use cover-fit textures, and the captions stay DOM text beneath each picture at 17px. On hover a plane scales 1.04 and a ripple follows the pointer for 600ms. Colour roles: flat ground, the pictures bring the colour, ink for captions. Variant: one fixed canvas draws every picture of the page as such a plane on its hidden DOM box (cover fit, a 16px radius in the shader, a parallax of plus or minus 8% of its height by scroll position, at most 8 planes active), all text staying real DOM, with plain images as the fallback when the frame rate drops.
phone: Bend at 40%, no hover; with reduced motion render plain DOM images.
houseRuleCheck: No colour split and no glow; pictures must not be documentary photographs.

name: Planes drift, photo covers
description: A hero made of drifting picture planes. 8 to 12 image planes (180 to 420px wide, designed or generated pictures with soft crops) hang in a field at different depths around a centred title (display 120px, up to three words). During the first 360px of scroll (scrubbed) the planes drift upward at depth-dependent speeds (0.4x to 1.6x of the scroll) while the title lifts and fades; at 360px the first full-bleed photograph of the next section (cover fit, 100vw by 90vh, 48px radius on the top corners) slides up over them as a sheet, so the planes are covered rather than scrolled away. Colour roles: ground flat, the planes carry the colour, the title in ink.
phone: 6 planes at 120 to 260px; title 64px; range 280px.
houseRuleCheck: The hero fills the first screen alone (the cover sheet appears only on scroll). No text boxes on the planes.

name: Cinematic post pass
description: One full-screen WebGL canvas (the hero or a stage section only, never the whole page) renders its scene to a texture and passes it through a two-stage chain. First a colour grade: contrast 1.1, saturation between 0.9 and 1.15, one temperature push toward the accent colour. Then film grain at 3-6 percent amplitude, re-seeded 24 times a second (or a 4x4 ordered dither at 1.5 percent). There is no channel split, no vignette and no bloom glow. The canvas runs at a pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and drops to grain only below 40fps. All type over the stage is HTML outside the pass, so letters stay crisp; the pass changes only the picture. Ground and ink come from the scene; the accent shows through the grade. Phone: grain and grade stay, pixel ratio 1.
phone: Grain and grade only, pixel ratio 1.
houseRuleCheck: Grade and grain only: a vignette (a gradient), bloom (a glow) and a red-blue lens split (an RGB ghost) are all left out. No glass, no overlay boxes.

name: Shader scene transition
description: Two full-screen scenes (pictures, clips or sections rendered to textures) blend through a fragment shader driven by a progress value 0-1: a noise-threshold dissolve, a liquid warp or a depth-mask wipe, with no colour split. The 3-6 scenes sit on a held stage of about one screen each: when the scroll crosses a scene's midpoint the blend plays over 1.0-1.4s as a timed step, and a filled next pill or the arrow keys do the same; the wheel itself is never captured. Each scene is full-bleed with a 56-110px headline at bottom-left and a 17px link; the outgoing text fades over 300ms and the incoming text rises after 600ms. Headline ink is white or near-black per scene luminance. Colour roles: scenes carry their own colour, accent none.
phone: Native scroll crosses the same midpoints, shader resolution 0.75, headline 40-52px; with reduced motion use a 300ms crossfade.
houseRuleCheck: The frost variant looks like glass and is dropped; use dissolve, liquid or depth-mask only, and no gradient overlay between scenes; no colour split, and no wheel capture.

name: Reel tilts up on hover
description: A media card whose reel plays on hover. Card 440x300 (radius 20, tint fill) with a poster still (the first frame) in a 400x240 frame at the top and a 22px title with one line of 16px text below. The reel (video or an animated picture) sits in the frame and on hover tilts up from rotateX(38deg) scale(0.95) opacity 0 to rotateX(0) scale(1) opacity 1, perspective 1000px, transform-origin at the bottom edge, 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), playing from the start; leaving reverses it over 350ms and pauses. Colour roles: card tint = ground, ink for the title, accent for at most one link.
phone: No hover: the reel tilts up and plays once when the card is 60% in view, one card at a time.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict: no text boxes on the reel, and the card is a fill.

name: Arrow nudges diagonally
description: The micro-motion on a button or link that ends in an arrow (the typeface's own arrow glyph, not an icon set). On hover or focus the arrow translates up and right by 2.6px (translate(2.6px, -2.6px), 200ms ease-out) and returns on leave; the label stays still. The button's fill shifts one tone step in 300ms (ground to ink, or a tint to a stronger tint) instead of an outline inversion. Works on pills and rectangles from 44 to 64px high; keep the arrow at 0.9em. Colour roles: fill and label ink, nothing else.
phone: Plays on tap down; no persistent hover state.
houseRuleCheck: A fill shift, not an outline inversion: outlined pills are banned.

name: Caption foot rises
description: A row of three or four filled photo cards at 1440, each 360 to 420px wide at 4:5 with a 20px radius and 24px gaps. At rest the picture fills the card down to a 56px foot in the card fill that holds a one-line title at 20px medium and a typeset arrow glyph at the right. On hover the foot grows by 130px (expo-out, 450ms) while the picture slides up inside the card by the same amount, so the foot never covers the photograph; after 120ms a two-line paragraph at 15px fades in with the arrow turning to the diagonal. Colour roles: card fill a tint of the ground, ink for text, accent only on the arrow. On a phone the cards go one per row at 100 percent minus 32px, the foot is permanently open with the paragraph visible, and no animation runs.
phone: One card per row, foot permanently open with the paragraph shown; no hover motion.
houseRuleCheck: Rewritten from an overlay panel on the photograph (a box on a photograph): the panel is now the card's own foot and the picture moves up as it rises, so nothing sits on the image. Arrow is a typeset glyph, no icon on top of the card. Use in one section so the page is not only boxes.

name: Button fill inverts
description: A button 56px high, 28-32px side padding, one corner treatment per site (square, 14px radius or full pill), 17-18px label at weight 500, sentence case. At rest it is filled with a soft tone of the page (ground stepped 6-10% darker or lighter) and ink text, with no outline. On hover the whole fill changes at once to solid ink and the label to the ground colour, a plain colour swap over 200-240ms with nothing travelling (a fill that sweeps across is a different pattern). Pressed: scale 0.98 for 90ms. Keyboard focus shows the hover state plus a 3px accent ring offset by 3px. Colour roles: ground, ink; accent appears only in the focus ring and, once per page, on the primary button's fill.
phone: No hover on touch: the pressed state shows the inverted colours for 150ms; keep the 56px tap target and make the button full width inside a stacked form.
houseRuleCheck: This move is usually built on a transparent outlined button; outlines are banned, so the rest state is a soft fill and only the hover inverts it.

name: Fill sweeps across
description: On hover a fill the size of the element sweeps across it. The fill (accent or ink, optionally skewed 8-12 degrees so its leading edge is diagonal) enters from the left (translateX -101 percent to 0) in 525ms on cubic-bezier 0.625, 0.05, 0, 1, and the label's colour inverts to the ground colour in step: the label has two copies, one rolling up out of a mask and the other rolling in from below. An arrow chip nudges 5px to the right. On leave the fill exits to the right (0 to 101 percent), so the motion always travels left to right. It suits 48-56px buttons (fully rounded or 12px radius), nav links with a 36px fill and list rows. Phone: no hover; the pressed state fills in 250ms from the touch side.
phone: No hover; press fills in 250ms.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Flat fill, no gradient edge, no outline.

name: One house easing
description: One timing pair is defined once as variables on the root and used for every hover, focus, open, close and entrance on the page: a single strong ease-out such as cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) and a single duration chosen per site (240, 400 or 560ms). Large entrances may use the same curve at 1.6x the duration. No linear, no browser default ease, no second curve. The choice sets the character: a quick-out at 240ms feels crisp and technical, a long in-out at 600ms feels soft and expensive. Scroll-linked smoothing and library tweens read the same numbers so everything on the page moves as one family. Colour roles: none. It is invisible, but it is the difference between a page that is built and a page that is assembled.
phone: Same tokens with durations at 0.8x; hover timings are not needed on touch, press and open timings keep the curve.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict. It is a token, not an effect, so it can sit under every other motion pattern.

name: Arrow exits and re-enters
description: A button 56px tall (pill or 14px radius), label 17px medium at the left, and at the right a 40px chip in the accent that holds a typeset arrow glyph, clipped by the chip. On hover the arrow slides out of the chip to the right (100 percent of the chip, 350ms expo-out) while a copy slides in from the left through the same chip; the label nudges 6px to follow. Colour roles: button fill the ink, label in the ground colour, chip in the accent with ink arrow. On a phone there is no hover, so the swap runs once on press and once when the button first enters the viewport.
phone: Swap runs on press and once on first view; button spans the width minus 32px.
houseRuleCheck: Clean: solid fill, no outline, no shadow; the arrow is a typeset glyph rather than an icon above a card.

name: Indent with dot
description: For rows or links in a list (a menu sheet, a project list, a footer link list) set at 28-72px with 14-20px between rows. On hover the label moves right 15-40px (about 0.5em, so 40px at the h2 step, 15-20px at the h4 step) over 400-500ms on the house ease-out (no overshoot) while a 10-24px dot in the accent scales from 0 to 1 in the space it leaves at the left. The ink does not change. The other rows stay still or dim to 0.5 (dealt per page). On leave it reverses in 300ms. Keyboard focus triggers the same state. The dot is a plain CSS disc, never an icon. Phone: there is no hover, so the row nearest the middle of the viewport (or the tapped row) shows the dot and the indent and the others rest.
phone: No hover: the row nearest the viewport middle, or the tapped one, shows the dot and indent.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The dot is a CSS disc, not a drawn shape or an icon; rows are separated by space, never by hairline dividers, and are not boxed.

name: Label roll-up
description: The label of a button or link sits in an overflow-hidden slot one line high (line-height 1.2; 17-18px label in a 56px button). A duplicate of the label waits directly beneath. On hover both move up 100% over 380-480ms on the house curve, so the label leaves through the top while its twin enters from below. The twin may take the accent or the inverted ink. Optional extras: the button grows 4% wider, or a text arrow glyph turns 45 degrees. Keyboard focus triggers the same roll. Sentence case, weight 500, tracking 0. Use on the primary button and the navigation links only, never on every text link. Colour roles: ground, ink, accent for the twin label.
phone: No hover on touch: play the roll on press (240ms); buttons full width; with reduced motion swap the label instantly.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; the arrow is a typed glyph, not a drawn icon.

name: Lift on hover
description: A button 56px tall (pill or 12px radius) whose rest fill is a soft tint of the ground. On hover it rises 3px (translateY, 400ms ease-out) while the fill fades to the full accent and the label shifts to the ink that reads on it; on press it returns to 0 in 120ms. On a phone it runs on the active press state only. This is the plain default hover; use it for secondary buttons when another special treatment already carries the page.
phone: Runs on the press state; no hover assumed.
houseRuleCheck: Clean provided the lift adds no drop shadow and the rest state is a filled tint, not an outline.

name: List hover backdrop clip
description: A list of 5-10 names (h1 step, 64-112px, left-aligned from the margin, no dividers) fills a 100svh section on the ground. Hovering a name plays that name's clip (muted, looped, or a still) full-bleed behind the list at 35-50 percent opacity, cross-fading in 300ms when the pointer passes between names and hiding 150ms after it leaves. The hovered name stays at full ink while the others dim to 0.45 over 250ms; there is no inverted band or box over the clip. Clips are 5-8s loops, 1080p, 2-3MB each, preloaded on the first hover. Phone: no hover; the list scrolls and the name in the middle of the viewport plays, the others dimmed.
phone: The name nearest the viewport middle plays, others dimmed.
houseRuleCheck: Clean when nothing boxes the row: an inverted white band over the clip would be a box on a photograph, so the siblings dim instead and the letters sit straight on the dimmed clip. No hairline dividers.

name: List dims, window glides
description: A list of five to eight lines, each 72 to 96px tall, set in display type at 56 to 72px from the left margin (120px) across about 800px at 1440. In the right third a picture window 360 x 460 with a 20px radius sits in a fixed column. Hovering a line dims all other lines to 0.45 opacity and glides the window vertically to the centre of that line (950ms expo-out); on arrival the picture crossfades to that line's image (250ms). Colour roles: ink on a flat ground, dimmed ink for the rest; no accent on the words. On a phone the lines stack at 36px; a tap marks a line active and opens its picture inline below it (an accordion about 280px tall) with no window and no dimming.
phone: Lines stack at 36px; a tap opens that line's picture inline as an accordion.
houseRuleCheck: The list starts at the left margin and the window takes the right third, so no row is empty on the left; lines are plain text with no divider rules or outlined boxes; pictures are styled, not documentary.

name: Media zooms in frame
description: Inside a card (a picture or a video, 16-24px radius, overflow hidden) hover scales the media to 1.05-1.1 over 400ms (cubic-bezier 0.3, 0.58, 0.41, 1) while the card itself stays still or shrinks to 0.95, so the frame appears to breathe. Text under or on the card does not move. It reverses in 400ms. Phone: no hover; the card nearest the middle of the viewport takes the 1.05 state while it is there.
phone: The card nearest the viewport middle takes the 1.05 state.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No outlines on the card, no shadow appearing on hover.

name: Neighbours part on hover
description: A centred row of four or five filled cards (280 x 400 at 1440, 20px radius, 16px gaps, flat fills from two or three palette colours) with a title at 24px. Hovering one card makes its neighbours slide 150px away on each side (expo-out, 700ms) so the hovered card can widen to 520px; after 200ms its description (two lines, 16px) fades in. Leaving reverses it in 500ms. Colour roles: fills from the palette, ink text, accent only on the open card's link. On a phone the cards stack as an accordion; a tap opens a card to reveal the description and pushes the next card down by about 150px.
phone: Accordion of cards; a tap opens one and pushes the next down.
houseRuleCheck: Cards carry their own fill, no outline, no shadow; keep to a single row so the page is not only boxes; cards may hold a picture but not text on a photograph.

name: Fill shape shrinks
description: A button 56px tall (pill or 12px radius) built from two layers: a fill layer in the accent and a label layer at 17px medium. On hover the fill layer scales to 98 percent about its centre (250ms ease-out) while the label stays perfectly still, so the shape looks pressed in; on leave it returns in 250ms. Colour roles: accent fill, label in the ink that reads on it. On a phone it runs on the press state only. A quiet default; use it where the page already has a louder moment.
phone: Runs on press; same geometry.
houseRuleCheck: Clean: solid fill, no outline, no shadow.

name: Pill appears around
description: Hover or focus on a nav word or button makes a solid pill appear behind it: 36-44px tall with 10px 18px padding, fully rounded, filled with the accent mixed 14-20 percent into the ground (or solid accent with ground-coloured letters), opacity 0 to 1 and scale 0.9 to 1 in 150-250ms. The current page keeps its pill and its label goes up 200 in weight without reflow (the width is reserved by a hidden bold copy). A shared pill that glides from item to item (300ms, expo-out) can replace per-item pills. Phone: no hover; the current item keeps the pill.
phone: No hover; the current item keeps the pill.
houseRuleCheck: Clean when solid: an outlined ring with a glow would break two bans, so the pill is a solid fill with no glow or outline.

name: Scale up on hover
description: Hover grows a button, or its inner label or chip, by 7-10 percent (scale 1.07-1.1, 150-250ms ease-out, origin at the centre) with the fill unchanged; press shrinks it to 0.97 for 100ms. Only transform is used, so neighbours do not move. Best on round buttons (a 56px disc or a pill action). Phone: only the press state.
phone: Press state only.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No shadow appears on hover.

name: Siblings dim
description: Hovering one link, button or chip in a group (a footer link list at 18-24px, a row of three to six buttons or 56px discs) dims the others: opacity 1 to 0.45 over 250ms linear, or the discs' fill to a flat grey tint and scale 0.9 over 300ms; the hovered one stays at full strength. The group has 24-40px gaps. Phone: nothing on touch; focus-visible gives the same dimming.
phone: None on touch; focus-visible only.
houseRuleCheck: Clean.

name: Tilted thumb tilts more
description: A loose collage of three to five thumbnails (240 to 320px wide, 4:5 or 1:1, 16px radius) laid along a row, overlapping at the corners by about 24px, each at rest turned a different amount (-4, 3, -2 degrees). Hovering one rotates it 2 degrees further in its own direction and grows it 5 percent on a critically damped spring (stiffness about 300, damping 35, roughly 450ms, no overshoot) and raises it above its neighbours so it reads as picked up. Colour roles: a flat ground with the pictures carrying the colour. On a phone the tilts stay, the thumbnails sit two per row with 16px margins, and a thumb does the same spring when it crosses the viewport centre or is tapped.
phone: Two per row, tilts kept; spring fires at viewport centre or on tap.
houseRuleCheck: Overlap only at corners; no shadow when lifted; no captions or boxes on the photographs; use styled or product pictures rather than documentary ones.

name: Subtle tint shift
